author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rhode Island had recorded 61,488 primary ballots by 9 a.m. Wednesday, equal to 7.8% of registered voters, according to Ocean State Media’s election coverage. The figure includes ballots cast before Election Day as well as the first two hours of in-person voting.

More than 37,000 Rhode Islanders voted early, over twice the early-vote total reported for the 2022 primary. That head start means the morning count should not be read as an Election Day-only measure or used by itself to forecast the final turnout.

Most polling places opened at 7 a.m. and are scheduled to close at 8 p.m. Mail ballots must also arrive by 8 p.m. to be counted, subject to state election rules. Voters can confirm their polling location through the Rhode Island secretary of state.

The 2022 primary drew total turnout of 44.4%, providing historical context but not a prediction for Wednesday. The 61,488 figure is a time-stamped snapshot and will change as election officials post additional in-person, early and mail-ballot data through the evening.
dek: Early voting helped lift the morning total as polling places opened statewide for Rhode Island’s September 9 primary.
headline: Rhode Island primary turnout reaches 61,488 by 9 a.m.
